Fears of return to all out US-Iran war after sharp escalation in deadly strikes | BBC News
recentItems.description:
Iran and the United States have carried out on the biggest exchange of attacks since July, stoking fears of a return to all out war.

Iran said 18 people were killed and more than 100 injured in latest US bombardment.  It accused the US of committing a war crime by striking a wedding in the city of Kuhestak, killing four people including two children. The Pentagon responded by saying it does not target civilians. 

In retaliation,  Iran launched a wave of strikes against American targets in the region, including in Kuwait, Jordan, Iraq and Bahrain. 

President Trump is warning that the US is prepared to carry out further strikes in response to those attacks. 

There are warnings of a serious impact on the global economy, with further disruption to oil and gas supplies, affecting inflation and global borrowing costs. 

Clive Myrie presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Caroline Hawley and Jeremy Bowen.

recentItems.title: Iran accuses US of war crimes after alleged strike on wedding | BBC News
recentItems.description:
The US and Iran have exchanged the largest number of strikes in weeks - after Iran retaliated to American attacks by launching strikes against US assets across the Middle East. 
 
Iran says one US strike hit a wedding celebration in the south of the county, killing four people including one child.
 
The US has denied targeting civilians but US Central Command says they're 'looking into' the strike.

Why did Apple Maps just rename Lake Ontario? | BBC News
recentItems.description:
Apple has renamed Lake Ontario as Lake America on its Maps app, after an order from US President Donald Trump.
 
It's all part of Washington's trade row with Canada.
 
The change was made for US-based users - those in Canada will continue to see Lake Ontario displayed. The BBC has contacted Apple for comment.

recentItems.title: What has Nigel Farage said on money, Andy Burnham and a 'complainants society'? | BBC Newscast
recentItems.description:
Today, Andy Burnham faced his first PMQs, and Nigel Farage has told Chris the UK is a "complainants' society" after questions about Reform’s funding.   

Adam and Chris unpack Chris’ first interview with Nigel Farage after he returned to parliament as the re-elected MP for Clacton on Tuesday. 

They discuss his response to continuing questions about the £5m he received from a crypto billionaire before becoming an MP, plus whether Andy Burnham’s premiership is a threat to Reform. Farage has said the £5m was a personal gift and did not therefore require registration under the rules.  

And Andy Burnham has faced Kemi Badenoch in his debut appearance at PMQs. Does the new Prime Minister seem like a breath of fresh air, or is it already a return to politics as usual?
